sources.publicConcepts: Untrusted data can flow from sources to sinks through assignments and calls. Configurable sanitizers affect flow. Exact source and sanitizer models distinguish call results from nested expressions; richer side-effect, control and cross-function analyses have separate contracts.

provenance: Public documentation concepts only. No upstream implementation or test-suite files opened, and no documentation source examples copied. All native API policies, fixtures and tests are original; these observations do not establish product compatibility, execution parity or security accuracy.

nativePolicy.optIn: A rule sets controlFlow to "branch-joins". Omitted or "straight-line" keeps straight-line-call-models-v1; switching methods requires a reviewed baseline migration.
nativePolicy.joins: if/else, standalone lexical blocks, conditional expressions and &&/||/?? evaluate the condition once, then trace both possible arms with independent bindings; the join keeps the union of possible origins. A sanitizer clears taint only if every continuing arm clears it. Returning arms report inside the arm and do not reach later statements.
nativePolicy.limits: 256 conditional forks per file shared across rules and at most 32 nested control/lexical scopes. Forks charge binding and trace copies to the existing work budget.
nativePolicy.refusals: Loops, local function declarations, nested var, binding shadowing, reads before declaration, unknown or dynamic calls and exhausted budgets refuse analysis, discard partial findings and mark the report incomplete.
nativePolicy.remaining: Feasibility proofs, predicate correlation, constant-branch pruning, implicit control taint, loops, exceptions, closures, heap/type/framework semantics, interprocedural analysis, documented competitor cases and comparative precision/recall remain unsupported.

refusals: example/branch-flow: Taint analysis: unsupported unmodeled or dynamic call
example/branch-flow: Taint analysis: var in a nested block
